title: Apply the ancient rules for acquiring and inheriting enslaved foreigners
topic: Land, harvests and provision for the poor
original_audience: Israelite households holding foreign slaves
verse_text: [25:44] And your male slave and your female slave, as many as you have from the nations which are round about you: from them you may acquire a male slave and a female slave. [25:45] And you may also acquire from the sons of the lodgers among you and from their relatives who come to be in your land; they shall become your possession. [25:46] And you shall distribute them to your children after you, and they shall be held by you permanently. But among your brethren, the sons of Israel, no one shall wear down his brother with toils.
maimonides: P235: Keep Canaanite slaves in permanent service

title: Permit redemption of an Israelite sold to a foreigner and calculate it by years remaining
topic: Land, harvests and provision for the poor
original_audience: Israelites sold to foreigners, their kin, and their purchasers
verse_text: [25:48] after he is sold to him, he shall have a right of redemption. One of his brethren may redeem him, [25:49] his father’s brother or the son of his father’s brother may redeem him, or one of his close kin from his tribe may redeem him; but if, having prospered by his hands, he redeems himself, [25:50] then he shall calculate with the one who acquired him from the year he sold himself to him until the year of release. His sale price shall be like a hired worker’s pay; he shall be with him year by year. [25:51] If many years remain for someone, he shall repay his redemption from his sale money in proportion to them. [25:52] If few years remain until the year of release, he shall calculate with him according to his years and repay his redemption.

title: Do not let a foreign owner work an Israelite harshly
topic: Land, harvests and provision for the poor
original_audience: Israel
context_note: the Lord through Moses addresses Israel in this passage.
verse_text: [25:53] He shall be with him as a hired worker year by year; you shall not wear him down with toil before you.
maimonides: N260: Do not let a gentile owner work a Hebrew servant harshly

title: Release the unredeemed Israelite and his children at Jubilee when held by a resident foreigner
original_audience: Resident foreign householders holding Israelite bonded workers, with the Israelite and his children as beneficiaries
context_note: Verse 54 supplies the fallback release even when the redemption in verses 48–52 has not occurred. C0733 covers the separate Israelite-master case in verse 41. C0737 states the redemption calculation.
verse_text: [25:54] If he is not redeemed by these means, he shall go out in the year of release, he and his children with him.

title: Do not erect an idolatrous pillar
original_audience: Israel
verse_text: [26:1] You shall not make for yourselves images made by hand, neither carved images, nor shall you set up a pillar for yourselves, nor place a conspicuous stone in your land to bow down unto it; I am the Lord your God.
maimonides: N11: Do not set up a pillar for worship

title: Do not place a figured stone for worship
original_audience: Israel
verse_text: [26:1] You shall not make for yourselves images made by hand, neither carved images, nor shall you set up a pillar for yourselves, nor place a conspicuous stone in your land to bow down unto it; I am the Lord your God.
maimonides: N12: Do not bow down on a figured stone

title: Apply the prescribed person-vow valuations, including the poor person's assessment
original_audience: Israelites making person-vows and priests assessing them
verse_text: [27:2] Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: Whosoever vows a vow for the valuation of his soul unto the Lord, [27:3] the valuation of a male from twenty to sixty years old shall be fifty didrachmas of silver, by the sacred weight. [27:4] For a female the assessed value shall be thirty didrachmas. [27:5] From five to twenty years old, the valuation shall be twenty didrachmas for a male and ten didrachmas for a female. [27:6] From one month to five years old, the valuation shall be five didrachmas of silver for a male and three didrachmas for a female. [27:7] From sixty years old and upward, the valuation shall be fifteen didrachmas of silver for a male and ten didrachmas for a female. [27:8] But if he is too poor for the valuation, he shall stand before the priest, and the priest shall value him; the priest shall value him according to the strength of the hand of the one who vowed.
maimonides: P114: Apply the valuation laws for vowed persons

title: Do not exchange a consecrated sacrificial animal
original_audience: Israelites who have dedicated sacrificial animals
context_note: Verse 9 supplies the operative premise of the exchange rule in verse 10. A qualifying animal given to the Lord is already holy.
verse_text: [27:10] He shall not exchange it, good for bad or bad for good. If he does exchange it, animal for animal, both it and its substitute shall be holy.
maimonides: N106: Do not substitute another animal for a consecrated one

title: Treat both original and substituted sacrificial animals as holy
original_audience: Israelites who exchange a consecrated sacrificial animal
context_note: The holiness of the original eligible animal explains why the prohibition on substitution applies.
verse_text: [27:10] He shall not exchange it, good for bad or bad for good. If he does exchange it, animal for animal, both it and its substitute shall be holy.
maimonides: P87: A substitute for a consecrated animal is also holy

title: Treat the priest’s valuation of the specified vowed livestock or consecrated house as binding
original_audience: Israelite dedicators and priests appraising the specified livestock or houses
verse_text: [27:11] If it concerns any unclean livestock of a kind not presented as a gift unto the Lord, he shall set the animal before the priest. [27:12] And the priest shall value it, between good and bad. As the priest values it, so it shall stand. [27:14] And if a man consecrates his house as holy unto the Lord, the priest shall value it, between good and bad. As the priest values it, so it shall stand.
maimonides: P115: Apply the valuation laws for consecrated animals
P116: Apply the valuation laws for consecrated houses

title: Add a fifth when redeeming the vowed animal
original_audience: Israelite who redeems the vowed animal
verse_text: [27:11] If it concerns any unclean livestock of a kind not presented as a gift unto the Lord, he shall set the animal before the priest. [27:12] And the priest shall value it, between good and bad. As the priest values it, so it shall stand. [27:13] If he does redeem it, he shall add a fifth to its valuation.

title: Add a fifth when redeeming the consecrated house
original_audience: Israelite who redeems the consecrated house
verse_text: [27:14] And if a man consecrates his house as holy unto the Lord, the priest shall value it, between good and bad. As the priest values it, so it shall stand. [27:15] If the one who consecrated it redeems his house, he shall add a fifth of the silver of the valuation to it, and it shall be his.

title: Value a consecrated ancestral field by its seed and remaining Jubilee years
original_audience: Israelite ancestral field dedicator and assessing priest
verse_text: [27:16] If a man consecrates unto the Lord part of the field of his possession, the valuation shall be according to its seed: fifty didrachmas of silver for a kor of barley. [27:17] If he consecrates his field from the year of release, it shall stand according to its valuation. [27:18] If he consecrates his field later, after the release, the priest shall calculate the silver for him according to the years remaining until the year of release, and a deduction shall be made from its assessment.
maimonides: P117: Apply the valuation laws for consecrated fields

title: Add a fifth when redeeming the consecrated ancestral field
original_audience: Israelite who redeems a dedicated ancestral field
verse_text: [27:19] If the one who consecrated the field redeems it, he shall add a fifth of the silver to its valuation, and it shall be his.

title: Do not redeem the consecrated field after the stated disqualifying sale
original_audience: Israelite who dedicated the ancestral field
verse_text: [27:20] If he does not redeem the field and sells the field to another man, he shall no longer redeem it.

title: Assign the unredeemed consecrated field to the priest at Jubilee
original_audience: Priests and parties to the dedicated field
verse_text: [27:21] When the release has passed, the field shall be holy unto the Lord like land set apart. It shall become the priest’s possession.
maimonides: P145: Apply the laws of devoted (cherem) property

title: Assess and pay the prescribed value for a consecrated purchased field
original_audience: Israelite dedicator of a purchased field and assessing priest
verse_text: [27:22] If he consecrates unto the Lord part of a field he acquired, which is not part of the field of his inherited possession, [27:23] the priest shall calculate for him the total valuation from the year of release, and he shall repay the valuation on that day as holy unto the Lord.
maimonides: P117: Apply the valuation laws for consecrated fields

title: Return a consecrated purchased field to its original owner at Jubilee
original_audience: Israel
context_note: At Jubilee a purchased field consecrated by its buyer returns to the original holder. This differs from the valuation and payment provision in verses 22–23.
verse_text: [27:22] If he consecrates unto the Lord part of a field he acquired, which is not part of the field of his inherited possession, [27:23] the priest shall calculate for him the total valuation from the year of release, and he shall repay the valuation on that day as holy unto the Lord. [27:24] And in the year of release the field shall be returned to the man from whom he acquired it, whose possession the land was.

title: Use the prescribed sanctuary weight for valuations
original_audience: Priests and persons making the prescribed valuations
verse_text: [27:25] And every valuation shall be by sacred weights; the didrachma shall be twenty obols.

title: Do not vow as a new dedication a firstborn animal already belonging to God
original_audience: Israelite livestock owners
verse_text: [27:26] And every firstborn which is born among your livestock shall belong unto the Lord, and none shall consecrate it; whether calf or sheep, it is the Lord’s.
maimonides: N107: Do not transfer a consecrated animal to another offering

title: Redeem the unclean firstborn at its assessed value plus a fifth, or sell it at the valuation
original_audience: Israelite owner of an unclean firstborn animal
verse_text: [27:27] If it is one of the unclean four-footed animals, he shall exchange it according to its valuation and add a fifth to it, and it shall be his. If he does not redeem it, it shall be sold according to its assessed value.

title: Do not sell an irrevocably devoted thing
original_audience: Israelite who irrevocably devotes property
verse_text: [27:28] But every devoted thing which a man dedicates unto the Lord, of all that he has, from man unto livestock, and from the field of his possession, he shall neither sell nor redeem; every devoted thing shall be most holy unto the Lord.
maimonides: N110: Do not sell a devoted (cherem) field or thing

title: Do not redeem an irrevocably devoted thing
original_audience: Israelite who irrevocably devotes property
verse_text: [27:28] But every devoted thing which a man dedicates unto the Lord, of all that he has, from man unto livestock, and from the field of his possession, he shall neither sell nor redeem; every devoted thing shall be most holy unto the Lord.
maimonides: N111: Do not redeem a devoted (cherem) field or thing

title: Do not ransom a person placed under the stated death devotion
original_audience: Israelite community under the stated devotion law
verse_text: [27:29] And whatsoever is devoted from among men shall not be redeemed, but shall surely be put to death.

title: Carry out the stated death devotion
original_audience: Israelites administering the stated legal judgment
verse_text: [27:29] And whatsoever is devoted from among men shall not be redeemed, but shall surely be put to death.

title: Set apart the prescribed tithe of produce and livestock as holy to God
topic: Land, harvests and provision for the poor
original_audience: Israelite produce growers and livestock keepers
verse_text: [27:30] Every tithe of the land, from the seed of the land and the fruit of trees, belongs unto the Lord; it is holy unto the Lord. [27:32] And every tithe of cattle and sheep, and everything that comes under the staff in the count—the tenth shall be holy unto the Lord.
maimonides: P78: Separate the tithe of cattle and sheep
P127: Separate the first tithe for the Levites
P128: Separate the second tithe for eating in Jerusalem

title: Add a fifth when redeeming the produce tithe
original_audience: Israelite who redeems part of the produce tithe
verse_text: [27:31] But if a man indeed redeems his tithe, he shall add a fifth part unto it, and it shall be his.

title: Do not exchange the tithe animal
original_audience: Israelite keeper presenting the animal tithe
verse_text: [27:33] You shall not exchange a good one for a bad one; but if you do indeed exchange it, its substitute also shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed.

title: Treat a substituted tithe animal as holy alongside the original
original_audience: Israelite keeper who substitutes a tithe animal
verse_text: [27:33] You shall not exchange a good one for a bad one; but if you do indeed exchange it, its substitute also shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed.
maimonides: P87: A substitute for a consecrated animal is also holy

title: Do not redeem the tithe animal or its substitute
original_audience: Israelite keeper presenting or substituting a tithe animal
verse_text: [27:33] You shall not exchange a good one for a bad one; but if you do indeed exchange it, its substitute also shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed.
maimonides: N109: Do not sell the animal tithe

title: Levites: carry the tabernacle and its furnishings in their assigned service
original_audience: Levites assigned to Tent service, through Moses
verse_text: [1:50] And you shall appoint the Levites over the Tent of Testimony, and over all its furnishings, and over all that is therein. They shall carry the Tent and all its furnishings, and they shall minister therein, and shall camp round about the Tent.
maimonides: P23: Levites perform their service in the sanctuary

title: Apply the stated death liability to unauthorized sanctuary intrusion
original_audience: Unauthorized persons approaching the sanctuary, with the charge kept by its appointed ministers
verse_text: [1:51] And when the Tent sets out, the Levites shall take it down; when it camps, they shall erect it. Let an outsider who approaches die.
maimonides: N74: A non-priest must not serve in the sanctuary

title: Levites: guard the tabernacle and its furnishings
original_audience: Levites assigned to guard the Tent, through Moses
verse_text: [1:53] But let the Levites camp before the Lord round about the Tent of Testimony, and there shall be no offence among the sons of Israel. And the Levites themselves shall keep the charge of the Tent of Testimony.
maimonides: P22: Guard the sanctuary (Levitical watch)
N67: Do not leave the sanctuary unguarded

title: Aaron and sons: keep the priestly charge of altar and inner sanctuary
original_audience: Aaron and his sons, through Moses
verse_text: [3:10] And you shall appoint Aaron and his sons over the Tent of Testimony, and they shall keep their priesthood, and all that concerns the altar and is within the veil. And the outsider who touches shall die.
maimonides: N67: Do not leave the sanctuary unguarded

title: The Levites belong to the Lord in place of Israel’s firstborn
original_audience: Moses as recipient of the Lord’s declaration, with the Levites and Israel’s firstborn affected
context_note: A direction recorded in this narrative. Its original speaker, recipient and occasion must be retained; recording an order does not establish that God approves it or commands every believer to repeat it.
verse_text: [3:12] And I, behold, I have taken the Levites from among the sons of Israel in place of every firstborn who opens the womb among the sons of Israel. They shall be their ransom, and the Levites shall be Mine. [3:13] For every firstborn is Mine. On the day when I struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated unto Myself every firstborn in Israel, from man unto livestock. They shall be Mine; I am the Lord.

title: Kohathites: do not touch the holy things themselves when carrying them
original_audience: Kohathite Levites carrying the holy things
verse_text: [4:15] And when the camp sets out, Aaron and his sons shall finish covering the holy things and all the holy utensils. Afterward the sons of Kohath shall enter to carry them, and they shall not touch the holy things, so that they do not die. These are what the sons of Kohath shall carry in the Tent of Testimony.

title: Kohathites: do not go in suddenly to look upon the holy things
original_audience: Kohathite Levites approaching the holy things
verse_text: [4:20] And they shall in no wise enter to behold the holy things suddenly, lest they die.

title: Exclude persons with the specified impurity from Israel’s sanctuary camp
original_audience: The congregation of Israel, through Moses
verse_text: [5:2] Command the sons of Israel to send out of the camp everyone with leprosy, everyone with a seminal discharge, and everyone unclean through a dead person. [5:3] From male unto female, send them outside the camp, and they shall in no wise defile their camps, wherein I dwell among them.
maimonides: P31: Send the ritually impure out of the camp (sanctuary)
N77: An impure person must not enter the sanctuary camp

title: Give the restitution to the priest when the injured person has no receiving kinsman
topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
original_audience: Israelite offenders owing restitution when there is no receiving next of kin
verse_text: [5:8] But if the man has no next of kin to receive repayment for the offence, the repayment made unto the Lord shall be the priest’s, besides the ram of atonement, wherewith he shall make atonement for him.

title: Give the prescribed firstfruits and sacred contributions to the priests
original_audience: Israelites bringing sacred contributions, with the priests as recipients
verse_text: [5:9] And every first portion from all the things consecrated among the sons of Israel that they bring unto the Lord, unto the priest, shall belong to him. [5:10] And each man’s consecrated things shall be his; whatsoever a man gives unto the priest shall be his.
maimonides: P126: Give the priest terumah from grain, wine and oil

title: Do not put oil or frankincense on the jealousy offering
topic: Marriage, family and care for parents
original_audience: The husband presenting the jealousy offering
verse_text: [5:15] then the man shall bring his wife unto the priest, and shall present the gift on her behalf, a tenth of an oiphi of barley flour. He shall pour no oil upon it, neither shall he put frankincense upon it; for it is a sacrifice of jealousy, a memorial sacrifice bringing sin to remembrance.
maimonides: N104: Do not put oil on the sotah's meal offering
N105: Do not put frankincense on the sotah's meal offering

title: Apply the stated jealousy law in the case it defines
original_audience: Israel, with the priest, the husband and the woman in the stated jealousy proceeding
context_note: A direction recorded in this narrative. Its original speaker, recipient and occasion must be retained; recording an order does not establish that God approves it or commands every believer to repeat it.
verse_text: [5:29] This is the law of jealousy, when a wife transgresses while under a husband and becomes defiled, [5:30] or when a spirit of jealousy comes upon a man and he is jealous of his wife. He shall set his wife before the Lord, and the priest shall perform all this law for her. [5:31] And the man shall be free from sin, and that woman shall bear her sin.

title: Nazirite: abstain from wine and strong drink
original_audience: Any Israelite man or woman who undertakes a Nazirite vow
verse_text: [6:3] from wine and strong drink, he shall be purified from wine. He shall drink neither vinegar of wine, nor vinegar of strong drink, nor anything prepared from grapes; and he shall eat neither fresh grapes nor raisins. [6:4] All the days of his vow he shall consume nothing made from the vine: wine, from pressed grape skins unto the seed.
maimonides: N202: Nazirite must not drink wine or grape-derived drink

title: Nazirite: abstain from wine vinegar and fermented-drink vinegar
original_audience: Any Israelite man or woman who undertakes a Nazirite vow
verse_text: [6:3] from wine and strong drink, he shall be purified from wine. He shall drink neither vinegar of wine, nor vinegar of strong drink, nor anything prepared from grapes; and he shall eat neither fresh grapes nor raisins. [6:4] All the days of his vow he shall consume nothing made from the vine: wine, from pressed grape skins unto the seed.
maimonides: N202: Nazirite must not drink wine or grape-derived drink

title: Nazirite: abstain from grapes and other vine products
original_audience: Any Israelite man or woman who undertakes a Nazirite vow
verse_text: [6:3] from wine and strong drink, he shall be purified from wine. He shall drink neither vinegar of wine, nor vinegar of strong drink, nor anything prepared from grapes; and he shall eat neither fresh grapes nor raisins. [6:4] All the days of his vow he shall consume nothing made from the vine: wine, from pressed grape skins unto the seed.
maimonides: N203: Nazirite must not eat fresh grapes
N204: Nazirite must not eat raisins
N205: Nazirite must not eat grape seeds
N206: Nazirite must not eat grape skins

title: Nazirite: let your hair grow and do not put a razor to it during the vow
original_audience: Any Israelite man or woman who undertakes a Nazirite vow
verse_text: [6:5] All the days of the vow of purification no razor shall come upon his head. Until the days which he vowed unto the Lord are fulfilled, he shall be holy, letting the hair of his head grow long.
maimonides: P92: Nazirite lets his hair grow
N209: Nazirite must not shave his hair

title: Nazirite: do not incur corpse defilement, even for close relatives
original_audience: Any Israelite man or woman who undertakes a Nazirite vow
verse_text: [6:6] All the days of his vow unto the Lord he shall not enter where any dead person is. [6:7] For his father, or his mother, or his brother, or his sister, he shall not defile himself when they die; for the vow of his God is upon him, upon his head.
maimonides: N207: Nazirite must not defile himself for the dead, even relatives
N208: A Nazirite must not enter a building containing a corpse

title: Nazirite: restart the vow period after defilement
original_audience: A Nazirite whose vow was interrupted by sudden corpse defilement
verse_text: [6:12] whereon he was consecrated unto the Lord for the days of the vow. And he shall bring a year-old lamb for a guilt offering; and the former days shall not be reckoned, for the head of his vow was defiled.

title: A Nazirite may drink wine again after completing the prescribed rite
original_audience: Israelite Nazirites completing the vow
context_note: The passage expressly restores permission after the offerings are presented. Existing C0811 governs abstention while the vow is active, and C0825 concerns the priest’s presentation and portions.
verse_text: [6:20] And the priest shall bring them as a presentation before the Lord. It shall be holy unto the priest, with the breast of presentation and the foreleg of the portion set apart; and afterward he who has vowed shall drink wine.

title: Nazirites: bring the gift undertaken in the vow of consecration
original_audience: Nazirites concerning their pledged gifts
verse_text: [6:21] This is the law of him who vows unto the Lord, his gift unto the Lord concerning the vow, apart from whatever his hand may find, according to the extent of his vow which he vows under the law of consecration.

title: Aaron and sons: bless Israel with the appointed words and God's name
original_audience: Aaron and his priestly sons, through Moses
verse_text: [6:23] Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons, saying: Thus you shall bless the sons of Israel, saying unto them (and they shall put My name upon the sons of Israel, and I, the Lord, will bless them): [6:24] The Lord bless you and keep you; [6:25] the Lord make His face shine upon you, and have mercy upon you; [6:26] the Lord lift up His face upon you, and give you peace.
maimonides: P26: Priests bless Israel with the priestly blessing

title: Observe the stated Levite entry, retirement and assistance ages
original_audience: Levites serving at the Tent and those assigning their service, through Moses
verse_text: [8:24] This concerns the Levites: from twenty-five years old and upward, they shall enter to work in the Tent of Testimony. [8:25] And from fifty years old he shall withdraw from the ministry, and shall work no longer. [8:26] And his brother shall minister in the Tent of Testimony, to keep the charges; but he shall perform no work. Thus you shall deal with the Levites in their charges.

title: Keep the second-month Passover when prevented by the specified uncleanness or journey
original_audience: Israelites and their descendants prevented by corpse uncleanness or a distant journey
context_note: Sabbath and festival observance remain disputed among Christians. This label does not declare Scripture abolished or prescribe a particular weekday of Christian worship.
verse_text: [9:10] Speak unto the sons of Israel, saying: If any man among you, or among your generations, is unclean through a dead person, or is on a distant journey, he shall observe the Passover unto the Lord. [9:11] In the second month, on the fourteenth day, toward evening, they shall observe it. They shall eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
maimonides: P57: Slaughter the second Passover (Pesach Sheni) offering
P58: Eat the second Passover offering with matzah and bitter herbs

title: Do not neglect the Passover when clean and not travelling
original_audience: Israel
context_note: the Lord through Moses addresses Israel in this passage.
verse_text: [9:13] And if a man is clean, and is not on a distant journey, and fails to observe the Passover, that soul shall be destroyed from his people; because he did not present the gift unto the Lord at its appointed time, that man shall bear his sin.
maimonides: P55: Slaughter the Passover offering at its appointed time

title: Aaron's sons: sound the appointed trumpets
original_audience: Aaron’s sons serving as priests
verse_text: [10:8] And Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall blow the trumpets. This shall be an everlasting statute for you throughout your generations.
maimonides: P59: Sound trumpets over offerings and in times of trouble

title: Apply the same standing offering rule to native Israelites and resident sojourners
original_audience: Native Israelites and resident sojourners bringing the stated offerings, with the officiating priests
context_note: The rule expressly identifies both groups and calls it an everlasting law. C0857 describes the offering accompaniments. The rule here is for this offering setting, apart from the same-law rule for Passover.
verse_text: [15:13] Every native-born person shall do such things in this way when presenting offerings of sweet savour unto the Lord. [15:14] But if a sojourner who joins you in your land, or whosoever is among you throughout your generations, makes an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord, as you do, so shall the congregation do unto the Lord. [15:15] You shall have one law, both you and the sojourners joined unto you, an everlasting law throughout your generations. As you are, so shall the sojourner be before the Lord. [15:16] One law and one ordinance shall apply to you and the sojourner attached to you.

title: Give the first portion of the dough to God
original_audience: Israelites eating the bread of the land, through Moses
verse_text: [15:19] then it shall be, when you eat of the loaves of the land, that you shall take a portion, a gift set apart unto the Lord. [15:20] As the firstfruits of your dough, you shall set apart a loaf for a portion set apart; as a portion from the threshing floor, so you shall take it, [15:21] the firstfruits of your dough; and you shall give unto the Lord a portion set apart throughout your generations.
maimonides: P133: Separate challah from dough for the priest

title: Offer a year-old female goat for the individual inadvertent offense in this provision
original_audience: An Israelite or resident sojourner who sins inadvertently under this provision, with the priest officiating
context_note: The verse specifies a year-old female goat and one law for native and sojourner. C0859 describes the congregation’s distinct rite in verses 22–26. The separate Leviticus 4 provisions permit different offerings in their stated cases.
verse_text: [15:27] But if one soul sins unintentionally, he shall present one year-old female goat for sin. [15:28] And the priest shall make atonement before the Lord for the person who acted unintentionally and sinned unintentionally, making atonement for that person. [15:29] For the native among the sons of Israel, and for the sojourner joined unto them, they shall have one law for whosoever acts unintentionally.

title: Apply the stated judgment for defiant sin
original_audience: Israelites and sojourners
context_note: The provision applies to native Israelites and sojourners. It contrasts defiant contempt for God's word with the provisions for unintentional sin in the preceding verses.
verse_text: [15:30] And the soul that acts with a presumptuous hand, whether of the natives or of the sojourners, provokes God; that soul shall be destroyed from his people, [15:31] because he treated the word of the Lord as worthless, and scattered His commandments. That soul shall surely be wiped out; his sin is upon him.

title: Make the prescribed fringes at the corners of the garment
original_audience: Israelites throughout their generations, through Moses
verse_text: [15:38] Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: Let them make for themselves fringes upon the corners of their garments throughout their generations; and you shall put a blue thread upon the fringes of the corners.
maimonides: P14: Wear fringes (tzitzit) on four-cornered garments

title: No non-Aaronide may approach to offer incense
original_audience: Israelites outside Aaron’s priestly line
verse_text: [17:5] as a reminder to the sons of Israel that no outsider who is not a descendant of Aaron should approach to place incense before the Lord, so that he will not become like Korah and his faction, as the Lord had spoken through Moses.

title: Bear the assigned responsibility for sanctuary and priesthood
original_audience: Aaron, with duties assigned to his sons and his ancestral house
context_note: The Lord speaks directly to Aaron. Responsibility concerning holy things includes his ancestral house. Responsibility concerning the priesthood belongs to Aaron and his sons.
verse_text: [18:1] And the Lord said unto Aaron, saying: You and your sons and your father’s house shall bear the sins concerning the holy things; and you and your sons shall bear the sins concerning your priesthood.

title: Levites: do not usurp priestly access to the holy vessels and altar
original_audience: Levites serving under Aaron and his sons
verse_text: [18:3] And they shall keep your charges and the charges of the Tent; only they shall not approach the holy vessels and the altar, that neither they nor you may die.
maimonides: N72: Levites and priests must not do each other's work

title: Israelites outside the appointed service: do not approach the restricted sanctuary ministry
original_audience: Outsiders to the appointed Tent service, including unappointed Israelites
verse_text: [18:4] And they shall join you, and shall keep the charges of the Tent of Testimony according to all the ministries of the Tent; and the outsider shall not approach you.
maimonides: N74: A non-priest must not serve in the sanctuary

title: Aaron’s priestly house receives the prescribed holy contributions by everlasting ordinance
original_audience: Aaron and his descendants, with eligibility according to the kind of sacred contribution
context_note: The Lord directly entrusts firstfruits and sanctified gifts to Aaron, then gives regulations for consuming or allocating them in 18:9 onward. The passage group has the broad heading and individual later records concern particular shares or meals.
verse_text: [18:8] And the Lord spoke unto Aaron: And I, behold, have given you charge of the firstfruits; from all things sanctified unto Me by the sons of Israel, I have given them unto you for a share of honour, and unto your sons after you, an everlasting ordinance. [18:19] Every portion of the holy things which the sons of Israel set apart unto the Lord I have given unto you, and unto your sons and unto your daughters with you, an everlasting ordinance; it is a covenant of everlasting salt before the Lord for you and for your seed after you.

title: The reserved portions of the most holy offerings are allotted to Aaron and his sons
original_audience: Aaron and his sons, as recipients of the reserved portions
verse_text: [18:8] And the Lord spoke unto Aaron: And I, behold, have given you charge of the firstfruits; from all things sanctified unto Me by the sons of Israel, I have given them unto you for a share of honour, and unto your sons after you, an everlasting ordinance. [18:9] And this shall be yours from the consecrated holy offerings: from all their gifts, and from all their sacrifices, and from every guilt offering of theirs, and from all their sin offerings which they render unto Me; from all the holy things it shall be yours and your sons’. [18:10] You shall eat them in the most holy place; every male shall eat them, you and your sons; they shall be holy unto you.

title: Priests' clean household members may eat the presented gifts
original_audience: Aaron and his household
context_note: the Lord addresses Aaron and his household in this passage.
verse_text: [18:11] And this shall be yours, the firstfruits of their gifts: from all the presentations of the sons of Israel, I have given them unto you, and unto your sons and unto your daughters with you, an everlasting ordinance. Everyone clean in your house shall eat them.

title: Everything devoted in Israel belongs to the priests
original_audience: Aaron and his sons
context_note: the Lord addresses Aaron and his sons in this passage.
verse_text: [18:14] Everything devoted among the sons of Israel shall be yours.
maimonides: P145: Apply the laws of devoted (cherem) property

title: Redeem the firstborn of unclean livestock
original_audience: Aaron’s priestly household administering redemption, with Israelite owners presenting the firstborn
verse_text: [18:15] And everything that opens the womb of all flesh, which they present unto the Lord, from man unto livestock, shall be yours; but the firstborn of men shall surely be redeemed, and you shall redeem the firstborn of unclean livestock.

title: Do not redeem firstborn cattle, sheep or goats
original_audience: Aaron’s priestly household and Israelite owners of firstborn cattle, sheep or goats
verse_text: [18:17] But you shall not redeem the firstborn of calves, and the firstborn of sheep, and the firstborn of goats; they are holy. And you shall pour their blood against the altar, and you shall offer up the fat as an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord.
maimonides: N108: Do not redeem firstborn clean animals

title: Give the clean firstborn sacrificial meat to the priest
original_audience: Aaron and his priestly household as recipients of the firstborn sacrificial meat
verse_text: [18:18] And their flesh shall be yours; as the breast of the presentation and the right foreleg, it shall be yours.

title: Do not assign Aaron's and Levi's tribe an ordinary territorial inheritance
original_audience: Aaron and the Levites concerning ordinary territorial inheritance
verse_text: [18:20] And the Lord spoke unto Aaron: You shall not inherit in their land, neither shall you have a portion among them; for I am your portion and your inheritance among the sons of Israel.
maimonides: N169: Levites must not receive a territorial inheritance
N170: Levites must not take a share of war spoils

title: Give Israel's service tithe to the Levites
original_audience: Israelites who set apart tithes, with the Levites as beneficiaries
context_note: Hebrews explicitly calls tithe collection a legal command and uses it as the comparison for Abraham’s payment to Melchizedek. The underlying Levitical provision remains in Numbers.
verse_text: [18:21] And to the sons of Levi, look, I have given every tithe in Israel as an allotment in return for their ministries, the service they perform in the Tent of Testimony.
maimonides: P127: Separate the first tithe for the Levites

title: Levites: set apart a tithe of the received tithe for the priest
original_audience: Levites receiving Israel’s tithe, through Moses
verse_text: [18:26] And you shall speak unto the Levites, and shall say unto them: When you receive from the sons of Israel the tithe which I have given you from them for an allotment, you shall take from it a portion set apart unto the Lord, a tithe of the tithe. [18:27] And your portions set apart shall be reckoned to you as grain from the threshing floor and as a portion set apart from the winepress. [18:28] Thus you shall also take of the portions set apart unto the Lord, from all your tithes which you receive from the sons of Israel; and from them you shall give a portion set apart unto the Lord unto Aaron the priest.
maimonides: P129: Levites give a tithe of their tithe to the priests

title: Levites and their households may eat their remaining tithe anywhere after setting aside its consecrated portion
original_audience: Levites receiving the tithe and their households
context_note: A direction recorded in this narrative. Its original speaker, recipient and occasion must be retained; recording an order does not establish that God approves it or commands every believer to repeat it.
verse_text: [18:31] And you shall eat it in every place, you and your households, for it is your wage in return for your ministries in the Tent of Testimony. [18:32] And you shall incur no sin through it, when you take the firstfruits from it; and you shall not profane the holy things of the sons of Israel, lest you die.

title: Use an unblemished red heifer that has never borne a yoke
original_audience: Israelites supplying the heifer through Moses and Aaron
verse_text: [19:2] This is the provision of the law which the Lord commanded, saying: Speak unto the sons of Israel, and let them bring unto you a red heifer without blemish, wherein is no defect, and upon which no yoke has been laid.
maimonides: P113: Prepare the red heifer and its ashes

title: The officiating priest and burner: remain unclean until evening
original_audience: The officiating priest and the person burning the heifer
verse_text: [19:7] And the priest shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. Afterward he may enter the camp, but the priest shall be unclean until evening. [19:8] And the one who burns it shall wash his clothes and bathe his body, and he shall be unclean until evening.

title: The ash gatherer: wash garments and remain unclean until evening
original_audience: The gatherer of the heifer’s ashes, under the ordinance for the Israelites and attached sojourners
verse_text: [19:10] And the one who gathers the heifer's ashes shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening. This shall be an everlasting ordinance for the sons of Israel and the attached sojourners.

title: Observe seven-day uncleanness after the specified human corpse, bone, grave or death-house contact
original_audience: Israelites and attached sojourners affected by the stated corpse contact
verse_text: [19:11] Whosoever touches a dead person, any human being who has died, shall be unclean for seven days.
maimonides: P107: Apply the laws of corpse impurity

title: Do not defile the Lord's tent by neglecting corpse purification
original_audience: Israel
context_note: the Lord through Moses and Aaron addresses Israel in this passage.
verse_text: [19:13] Whosoever touches the dead body of any human being who has died, and is not purified, has defiled the Tent of the Lord; that soul shall be wiped out from Israel. Because water of sprinkling was not sprinkled upon him, he is unclean; his uncleanness is still in him. [19:20] And if a man is defiled, and is not purified, that soul shall be destroyed from the midst of the congregation, because he has defiled the holy things of the Lord; because water of sprinkling was not sprinkled upon him, he is unclean.
maimonides: N77: An impure person must not enter the sanctuary camp

title: Treat the uncovered open vessel in the death-house as unclean
original_audience: Israelites and attached sojourners subject to death-house purity rules
verse_text: [19:15] And every open vessel without a fastening tied upon it is unclean.
maimonides: P107: Apply the laws of corpse impurity

title: Observe uncleanness until evening after the prescribed bathing
original_audience: The person being cleansed of corpse impurity on the seventh day
verse_text: [19:19] And the clean person shall sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. He shall be purified on the seventh day, wash his clothes, and bathe in water, and he shall be unclean until evening.

title: The person touching purification water: remain unclean until evening
original_audience: Anyone touching the purification water within Israel’s purification ordinance
verse_text: [19:21] And this shall be an everlasting ordinance for you. The one who sprinkles the water of sprinkling shall wash his clothes, and whosoever touches the water of sprinkling shall be unclean until evening.
maimonides: P108: Apply the laws of the purification (sprinkling) water

title: Apply the prescribed secondary-contact uncleanness rule
original_audience: Israelites and attached sojourners subject to impurity by secondary contact
verse_text: [19:22] And whatever the unclean person touches shall be unclean, and the person who touches it shall be unclean until evening.

title: Phinehas and his descendants hold the covenant of priesthood
original_audience: Phinehas son of Eleazar and his descendants, through the Lord’s message to Moses
context_note: The Lord gives an everlasting covenant of priesthood to the named line. This establishes the line’s enduring covenant status separately from the one-time commission to announce it in C1226.
verse_text: [25:13] And it shall be for him and his seed after him an everlasting covenant of priesthood, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the sons of Israel.

title: Assign inheritance by the prescribed order of descendants and nearest kin
original_audience: Israel administering inheritances, through Moses
context_note: The daughters cite the original ruling in Numbers 27 and receive their share. Link this documented application to the existing inheritance rule.
verse_text: [27:7] The daughters of Zelophehad have spoken rightly. You shall surely give them a possession of inheritance among their father’s brethren, and shall assign their father’s allotment unto them. [27:8] And you shall speak unto the sons of Israel, saying: If a man dies, and has no son, you shall assign his inheritance unto his daughter. [27:9] But if he has no daughter, you shall give the inheritance to his brother. [27:10] But if he has no brothers, you shall give the inheritance to his father's brother. [27:11] But if his father has no brothers, you shall give the inheritance to his nearest relative from his tribe, and he shall inherit his property. This shall be a rule of judgment for the sons of Israel, as the Lord commanded Moses.
maimonides: P248: Apply the Torah's order of inheritance

title: Present God's prescribed offerings at their appointed times
original_audience: The sons of Israel, through Moses
verse_text: [28:2] Command the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them, saying: You shall take care to present My gifts, My donations, My offerings of sweet savour unto Me at My feasts.

title: Offer the additional Sabbath lambs with the prescribed accompaniments
original_audience: Israel providing the Sabbath offerings, with sanctuary ministers officiating
verse_text: [28:9] And on the Sabbath day you shall bring two unblemished year-old lambs, and two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice, and a drink offering, [28:10] a Sabbath whole burnt offering on each Sabbath, besides the continual whole burning and its drink offering.
maimonides: P41: Bring the additional Sabbath offering

title: Offer the prescribed new-moon burnt and sin offerings with their accompaniments
original_audience: Israel providing the new-moon offerings, with sanctuary ministers officiating
verse_text: [28:11] And at the new moons you shall bring whole burnt offerings unto the Lord: two calves from the cattle, and one ram, and seven unblemished year-old lambs; [28:12] For each calf, three tenths of fine flour mixed with oil; for each ram, two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil; [28:13] For each lamb, a tenth of fine flour mixed with oil: a sacrifice, a sweet savour, an offering unto the Lord. [28:14] Their drink offering shall be wine: half a hin for each calf, a third of a hin for each ram, and a quarter of a hin for each lamb. This is the whole burnt offering month by month throughout the year. [28:15] And one male goat from the goats for sin unto the Lord; besides the continual whole burning shall it be offered, and its drink offering.
maimonides: P42: Bring the additional new-moon offering

title: Offer the prescribed Weeks burnt and sin offerings with their accompaniments
original_audience: Israel, with the sanctuary priests officiating at the Feast of Weeks
context_note: the Lord through Moses addresses Israel, with the priests officiating in this passage.
verse_text: [28:27] And you shall bring whole burnt offerings for a sweet savour unto the Lord: two calves from the cattle, one ram, seven unblemished year-old lambs. [28:28] Their sacrifice shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for each calf and two tenths for each ram; [28:29] a tenth for each of the seven lambs; [28:30] and one male goat for sin, to make atonement for you. [28:31] These are apart from the continual whole burnt offering. You shall prepare their sacrifice for Me—they shall be unblemished—and their drink offerings.
maimonides: P45: Bring the additional Shavuot offering

title: Do not profane or break your pledged word
original_audience: Israelite vow-makers, with Moses addressing the tribal heads
verse_text: [30:3] Any person who vows a vow unto the Lord, or swears an oath, or imposes a restriction upon himself, shall not profane his word. He shall do everything that comes from his mouth.
maimonides: P94: Fulfil whatever you vow or pledge with your lips
N157: Do not break one's vow or oath

title: Apply the stated confirmation or timely annulment rules to a young daughter's vow
original_audience: A young daughter in her father’s household and the father hearing her vow, through Israel’s tribal heads
verse_text: [30:4] If a woman vows a vow unto the Lord or imposes a restriction while in her father’s house in her youth, [30:5] and her father hears her vows and her restrictions that she imposed upon herself, but her father remains silent toward her, then all her vows shall stand, and all her restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain. [30:6] But if her father refuses her on the day he hears, none of her vows or restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall stand. The Lord will cleanse her, because her father refused her.
maimonides: P95: Apply the laws of annulling vows

title: Apply the stated confirmation, annulment and liability rules to a wife’s vow
original_audience: Israelite women marrying with a prior vow or vowing in a husband’s household, and the husbands who hear the vows, through Israel’s tribal heads
context_note: Numbers 30:7–9 concerns a woman who enters marriage with an existing vow. The linked verses 11–16 address vows made in the husband’s household and liability for later annulment.
verse_text: [30:7] If she becomes a man’s wife while her vows are upon her, according to the specific statement of her lips by which she imposed a restriction upon herself, [30:8] and her husband hears, and remains silent toward her on the day he hears, then all her vows shall stand, and her restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain. [30:9] But if her husband refuses her on the day he hears, none of her vows or restrictions that she imposed upon herself shall remain, because her husband refused her. The Lord will cleanse her.
maimonides: P95: Apply the laws of annulling vows
